resolutions.researcher_notes: CONTRADICTS THE SHEET. Recorded ProposalYear=2014/ProposalMonth=8 (August 2014); the dead current_ref was a generic elibrary.ferc.gov search URL, not a document. The actual FERC order for this exact docket (CP14-96-000) states, twice, that Algonquin filed the AIM Project application on February 28, 2014 — not August. ProposalYear=2014 is correct; ProposalMonth=8 appears to be wrong (should be 2/February). The order does contain an August 2014 date, but for a different milestone: 'Commission staff issued the draft EIS for the AIM Project on August 6, 2014' and 'Notice of the draft EIS was published in the Federal Register on August 12, 2014' (para. 53-54) — this looks like the likely source of the August confusion (draft-EIS notice date mistaken for the application/proposal date). Recommend correcting ProposalMonth to February (2). Flagging for validity review rather than silently changing the value.

Independently (government, second source) corroborates construction spanning 2015-2016, consistent with recorded ConstructionYear=2015, though again does not itself state a construction-start month.

verifications.note: Enbridge's own 'Energy Infrastructure Assets' factsheet (already staged on this row for Operator/__VALIDITY__), Algonquin Gas Transmission entry (p.69-70): 'Ownership: Enbridge (100% Algonquin Base Business membership interest and 85% Algonquin Incremental Market project membership interest); Eversource Energy (15% Algonquin Incremental Market project membership interest)'. Directly names the AIM project and gives an 85%/15% Enbridge/Eversource split for this specific segment, distinct from 100% Enbridge on the rest of the base system.

Eversource Energy 2018 Form 10-K, Note K (Investments): 'As of December 31, 2018 and 2017, Eversource's investments included ... a 15 percent ownership interest in a FERC-regulated natural gas transmission business of $155.0 million and $159.6 million, respectively.' Confirms the 15 percent figure from an independent regulatory filing by the other owner; the 10-K does not itself name 'Algonquin' or 'AIM' in this note (Eversource's only FERC-regulated gas transmission equity investment of this kind is its AIM stake, per the Enbridge factsheet and Eversource's other public AIM-shipper disclosures), so name_found is false for this record even though the value corroborates.

resolutions.researcher_notes: CONTRADICTS THE SHEET. Recorded Owner1=Enbridge/100% for this row (sheet row 11, the 'Algonquin Incremental Market (AIM) Gas Pipeline' segment specifically — not the base Algonquin system, which is separately 100% Enbridge). Enbridge's own factsheet states the AIM project specifically is 85% Enbridge / 15% Eversource Energy membership interest, and Eversource's 2018 10-K independently confirms a matching 15 percent ownership interest (valued at $155.0M/2018, $159.6M/2017) in a FERC-regulated gas transmission business. Two independent sources (the two counterparties themselves) agree on an 85/15 split, not 100% Enbridge, for this AIM-specific row. Recommend correcting Owner1%=85.00% and adding Owner2=Eversource Energy / Owner2%=15.00% on this row. Also checked the 2015 FERC order (para. 3): as of March 2015 Algonquin was 'an indirect, wholly-owned subsidiary of Spectra Energy Partners, LP' — pre-dates both the Enbridge/Spectra merger (Feb 2017) and, seemingly, the Eversource AIM equity stake, so it does not conflict with the 85/15 finding, it simply reflects an earlier ownership chain (Spectra, later Enbridge).
